ingredients.item: amchur, or the juice of half a lemon

steps.text: Warm the ghee in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle until fragrant.
Add the onions with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring now and then, until deep golden at the edges.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, and green chilli. Cook for a minute, until the raw smell has gone.
Add the coriander, cumin, turmeric, and cayenne. Stir for thirty seconds to bloom them in the fat.
Tip in the tomatoes and scrape the base of the pan clean as they loosen.
Cook the masala down until it darkens and the ghee beads at the edge of the pan.
Add the chickpeas and the salt, then pour in 250 ml of water and stir to loosen.
Crush a ladleful of the chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
Simmer uncovered until the gravy coats the chickpeas rather than pooling around them.
Stir in the garam masala and the amchur. Taste, and add salt until the flavours sharpen.
If it has gone tight, loosen with hot water; if it is loose, simmer a few minutes longer.
Take the pan off the heat and leave it covered so the chickpeas drink up the gravy.
Scatter over the coriander and serve with rice or flatbread.
